items.q: What happened to Claude Code merges from June to September?
items.a: Merged pull requests **more than doubled**. The share that had to be **reverted fell by more than 40%**. The mono repo went from about **2,500 merges a day in May** to **more than 30,000 by September**.

items.q: What is scarce once Claude writes about 90% of Claude Code?
items.a: **Human attention**, not code. Most pull requests should merge with **at most one person**, and that person can be the author. If reverts rise, the time moved from review to cleanup.

items.q: What must Claude show before anyone else looks?
items.a: Something it can run: **tests, a build, or a screenshot**. The engineer who created Claude Code estimates this makes the result **two to three times** better.

items.q: How does the agent review avoid posting every guess?
items.a: Several agents hunt. A **separate group votes**. A finding posts only if enough agree. Substantive comments went from **16% to 54%** of pull requests. **Open security findings block the merge**.

items.q: What stopped a pull request from looping all night?
items.a: One request went through **more than 50 rounds**. After **three rounds** the reviewer asks the author to rethink. Single-round passes then went from **65% to 78%**.

items.q: Which two rules does he say to copy first?
items.a: **An agent's approval never counts as a human's.** Whoever **prompted the agent owns the change**. The change sets the tier: trusted low-risk can skip an extra person, ordinary work needs one, the riskiest needs two.

items.q: Why does he not treat the headline numbers as settled?
items.a: Anthropic is **grading its own homework**. Nobody has checked them. It spends more on tokens than most businesses want, and the review product **only works with GitHub**.

items.q: Why did more writing make review slower everywhere else?
items.a: Pharos, on **more than 10,000 developers in 2025**, saw heavy AI teams merge **98% more** pull requests while review time rose **91%**. Claude Code built for that bottleneck and cut the revert share by almost half.

items.q: When is it too early to review less?
items.a: Until mistakes are cheap to undo: tests an agent can run, **feature flags**, staged release, fast rollback. He cites DORA 2025: only about **21% of teams** recover a failed deploy in **under an hour**.

items.q: What should leadership map before it fires coordinators?
items.a: Every decision by how much **human attention** it needs: none, a human **on the loop**, a human **in the loop**, or a **licensed signature**. Automate coordination first. Keep a human on the hook.

items.q: What does he measure a manager by, once agents do the reading?
items.a: **Span of accountability**, not span of control. Since September, GitHub lets **Copilot's approval** count toward a required approval. He would not copy that if you are regulated.
